editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the respiratory care assessment offered by NBRC, priced at $360 with a duration of 240 minutes, covering patient data and device management.
editorial.overview: The official respiratory care assessment is certified by the NBRC and serves as the primary evaluation replacing separate TMC and CSE evaluations starting January 1, 2027. Note that the CSE remains available through December 31, 2027 for candidates who pass TMC at the high cut score before December 31, 2026. Candidates complete the assessment over a duration of 240 minutes at a total exam price of $360 to earn professional credentials while meeting all criteria.
editorial.who_should_take: Advanced respiratory therapists and graduates of accredited respiratory care education programs who want to earn professional credentials. Candidates must meet specific age and education requirements before applying.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review detailed content outlines provided by the NBRC to understand the specific patient care settings and question topics in complete detail before your scheduled test date. Utilize official self-assessment exams and practice materials to carefully evaluate your performance and identify areas needing further study before exam day arrives.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain focuses extensively on reviewing medical records, conducting clinical assessments, and executing procedures needed to gather accurate information regarding a patient's overall respiratory status during care evaluations.
study_focus: Evaluate Data in the Patient Record
Perform Procedures to Gather Clinical Information

domain_guidance.summary: This specific domain covers the technical aspects of troubleshooting clinical devices during and after setup while maintaining strict safety standards and standard quality assurance protocols across various practice environments.
study_focus: Troubleshoot Devices During and After Assembling
Ensure Infection Prevention or Control, Safety, and Performance of Quality Assurance Procedures

domain_guidance.summary: This specific domain directly addresses standard therapeutic interventions such as maintaining artificial airways, executing lung expansion techniques, and supporting patient ventilation to improve clinical outcomes successfully during active medical care.
study_focus: Maintain a Patent Airway Including the Care of Artificial Airways
Perform Airway Clearance and Lung Expansion Techniques

domain_guidance.summary: This specific domain carefully evaluates the broad range of professional knowledge expected of candidates across general respiratory care topics and clinical practice environments to ensure complete competence before final certification.

This specific domain actively tests advanced clinical judgement abilities required to make appropriate decisions regarding patient management and treatment modifications in complex healthcare scenarios encountered by active practitioners.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive at the designated assessment center well in advance with proper identification. Make sure you manage your 240 minutes effectively across all scheduled examination questions during your session.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The certification assessment consists of multiple-choice items, and candidates should check with NBRC regarding the exact total count of scored and pretest questions administered during the test session.
Two cut scores determine whether you receive credentials as a CRT or as an RRT. Achieving the low cut score earns the CRT credential, while achieving the high cut score earns the RRT credential.
The exam is administered over a duration of 240 minutes, giving candidates ample time to complete all required sections and questions within the designated testing facility without feeling rushed.
The official exam price is set at $360 for applicants taking the assessment as announced by the NBRC for certification candidates seeking their professional credentials.

methodology.summary: This page was built using official NBRC exam guides and documentation to provide verified requirements, domain breakdowns, and structural details for the certification path.
